wildFeature.key: Trilithon: Two standing stones with a lintel on top.
Iron Pillar: Rusting cylinder humming faintly.

Grandfather Clock: Ticking loudly, perfectly clean.
Lone Boulder: A massive, unmovable rock.
Plush Carpet: An incredibly long red runner unrolled in the dirt.
Ruined Watchtower: Stone cylinder, roof missing.
Giant Anchor: Rusted iron hook the size of a house.

Terraced Slopes: Earth naturally shaped like giant stairs.
Towering Mesa: Steep-sided, flat-topped earth pillar.
Aqueduct Pillar: Massive stone support for a ruined water bridge.
Crumbling Corner: Two walls meeting at a 90-degree angle.
Balanced Rock: Massive boulder on a tiny pedestal.
Oasis / Hot Spring: A small pool of perfectly clear water.
Floating Weapon: A normal longsword, frozen 20 feet in the air.
Singing Crystals: Shards of quartz that hum in the wind.
Floating Rock Steps: 1d4+1 stones hovering like stairs.
Giant Chainmail: A single pauldron from a colossal suit of armor.
Whirlpool / Siphon: Water actively draining underground.
Wooden Blockhouse: Rotting timber fort.

Wrecked Galleon (Bow): The front half of a massive ship.
Hollow Rock: A boulder with a cave-like interior.
Bramble Wall: Impassable thicket of thorns.
Ghost Ship: An illusion of a ship that loops a 5-sec crash.
Executioner's Block: Stained wooden stump & basket.
Earthwork Trench: Defensive ditch and dirt berm.
Obsidian Pillar: Razor-sharp black glass.
Natural Amphitheater: A bowl-shaped depression.
Giant Shield: A 20-foot tall iron shield propped against a rock.

Split Boulder: A giant rock cracked perfectly in half.
Broken Stone Bridge: Center span has collapsed.

rows.key: Entertainment Strip
rows.note: UNMAPPED — taverns/theaters/gambling district; Site 10's brief covers civic/market, not entertainment.

rows.key: Harborfront
rows.note: UNMAPPED — docks/harbor infrastructure has no golden-site owner; adjacent to Site 10 but not named in its brief.

rows.key: Underworks
rows.note: sewers/undercity read as the concealed-layer condition (Site 8), not a standalone site noun.

rows.key: Market Ward
rows.note: direct — stalls/plaza are named Site 10 pieces.

rows.key: Civic Center
rows.note: direct — civic/institutional buildings are Site 10's core.

rows.key: Industrial Ward
rows.note: direct — workshop/forge vernacular.

rows.key: Ruined Quarter
rows.note: direct — 'ruined' is exactly the abandoned/condition site.

rows.key: Slums / Low Ward
rows.note: UNMAPPED — poverty district; not a named golden-site vernacular.

rows.key: Temple Ward
rows.note: urban-context religious building; Site 4 (Monastery/Commune) is the rural-commune expression of the same vernacular, not this district.

rows.key: Noble Quarter
rows.note: civic/residential district; loosely covered by Site 10's town vernacular.

rows.key: Subterranean Crypt
rows.note: funerary/tomb space; closest fit is the abandoned/condition family (full host kit + collapse), not a distinct golden site.

rows.key: Natural Cavern
rows.note: direct — 'natural' vernacular is Site 7's own.

rows.key: Military Fortification
rows.note: direct — military-masonry family; Site 1 Guard Post is the small end of the same vernacular.

rows.key: Infrastructure Hub
rows.note: UNMAPPED — aqueduct/utility hub; adjacent to Site 5's excavated vernacular but functionally a city-utility space, not extraction/craft.

rows.key: Sunken Estate
rows.note: a flooded/collapsed manor — the abandoned/condition family.

rows.key: Religious Sanctuary
rows.note: direct.

rows.key: Prison / Asylum
rows.note: direct.

rows.key: Laboratory / Workshop
rows.note: direct.

rows.key: The Living Hive
rows.note: direct — explicitly a living structure.

rows.key: The Megastructure
rows.note: closest fit is the titan-scale family; could equally read as Site 12 anomalous — genuinely ambiguous.
